tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/hold_lifecycle.py
  tests/test_hold_lifecycle.py

WHY — measured on a real episode today. The owner wants publishing to be hands-off: an episode is booked into a calendar slot and the five-minute publish drain picks it up and ships it. The queue itself WORKS (three episodes published through it). Two gaps break the hands-off promise, both confirmed:

GAP 1 — A HELD EPISODE NEVER RETURNS. Episode 104 failed content QA weeks ago and was parked at stage "awaiting-host-input". Its blockers have since cleared (show notes qa-approved, publish preflight 12 of 12, certification 10 of 10), but nothing moved it back onto the track, so the drain never saw it: the drain only selects episodes at stage "publish-queued". The only resume path, POST /webhook/host/resume in server/app.py, is a STUB that returns {"status": "resumed"} and changes no state. An episode can therefore sit held forever after its reason for being held is gone.

GAP 2 — STALE QA VERDICT BLOCKS FOREVER. publish_preflight.authorize_publish refuses with "content QA not pass: 'fail'" because orchestrator._content_qa_status reads a STORED verdict at ep._data["qa_results"]["content"]["passed"]. That verdict is from the old failed run. Content has been regenerated since, but the stored verdict was never invalidated, so the authorization gate reads a result that no longer describes the current content. A stale pass would be worse than a stale fail: it would authorize a publish on evidence about different content.

BUILD server/pipeline/hold_lifecycle.py — stdlib only, pure functions plus one orchestrating call. NO stage mutation inside the pure functions; the caller applies decisions.

  qa_verdict_is_current(ep_data, *, content_fingerprint) -> (bool, str)
      A stored QA verdict is CURRENT only when it records the fingerprint of the content it
      judged and that fingerprint matches the content now present. Return (False, reason)
      when the verdict has no fingerprint (legacy verdicts predate this and must be treated
      as STALE, never as current), when fingerprints differ, or when the verdict is absent.
      Reason strings must name which case fired.

  stale_verdict_status(ep_data, *, content_fingerprint) -> str
      Return "pass" / "fail" only when the verdict is current; return "stale" when it is not.
      A caller must never receive "pass" from a verdict that did not judge the current
      content. This is the fail-closed rule of the module.

  outstanding_blockers(ep_data) -> list[dict]
      Everything that would still hold the episode, each {"id","reason"}: open recording
      -context publish holds (status not in recording_context.NON_BLOCKING_HOLD_STATUSES),
      a show-notes block whose status is not approved/qa-approved, and a non-current or
      failing content QA verdict. Import NON_BLOCKING_HOLD_STATUSES from
      server.pipeline.recording_context rather than restating the set.

  resume_decision(ep_data, *, content_fingerprint, resume_stage="publish-queued") -> dict
      Returns {"resume": bool, "target_stage": str|None, "blockers": [...], "reason": str}.
      resume True ONLY when the episode is currently in a special stage AND
      outstanding_blockers is empty. Never propose a resume for an episode that is not held.
      Never propose a target stage other than resume_stage.

  apply_resume(ep, decision) -> bool
      The single place that mutates state. Calls ep.advance(decision["target_stage"]) and
      records an audit entry (timestamp, previous stage, the blockers that were checked and
      found clear) onto the episode data. Returns False without mutating when
      decision["resume"] is False. This function must be the ONLY mutation path.

TESTS (tests/test_hold_lifecycle.py; at least 6):
 (1) a held episode with zero outstanding blockers yields resume True targeting
     publish-queued, and apply_resume advances it and writes the audit entry;
 (2) NEGATIVE: a held episode with an OPEN recording-context hold yields resume False and
     names that hold in blockers; apply_resume mutates nothing;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a stored QA verdict with NO fingerprint is treated as stale, so
     stale_verdict_status returns "stale" (not "pass") even when passed is True — the
     fail-closed case that matters most;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a verdict whose fingerprint differs from current content returns "stale";
 (5) a verdict whose fingerprint matches returns "pass"/"fail" faithfully;
 (6) NEGATIVE: an episode NOT in a special stage never yields resume True, even with zero
     blockers (resuming a running episode would skip stages);
 (7) a hold with status resolved_by_edit does not count as a blocker, proving the shared
     status set is honoured rather than duplicated;
 (8) apply_resume returns False and mutates nothing when resume is False.
tasks.verified: a held episode whose blockers cleared can resume automatically, and a QA verdict that did not judge the current content is never read as a pass
